title: Sweep-and-Stitch rollout adapter with telemetry-driven cohort handover
author: Riley Chen
release_notes: Introduce Sweep-and-Stitch rollout adapter: a telemetry-first, cohort-handover mechanism for low-risk promotions and automated rollback triggers.
performance_impact: p95 latency +2-5ms in worst-case during handover windows; net cost neutral due to reduced failed-promote rework and improved cache reuse
description: Summary: Adds a new 'Sweep-and-Stitch' rollout adapter to the rollout orchestrator that performs a lightweight telemetry sweep on shadowed traffic and then stitches cohorts into live traffic with consistency latches. The adapter coordinates short-lived cohort handoffs, session fencing and a small staged drain window to avoid mid-session model swaps. Motivation: Existing promote/pause workflows rely on fixed step timers or simple metric gates which can either delay safe promotions or allow brittle promotes when signals are noisy. Sweep-and-Stitch treats promotion as a two-phase operation: 1) Sweep: send mirrored/shadow traffic slices to the candidate, collect rich telemetry (latency tail, token-level error proxies, structured output diffs, log-level warnings, and eval-set regressions), and compute cohort-specific risk scores. 2) Stitch: for cohorts that pass risk thresholds, perform an atomic cohort handover using a short consistency latch that maintains session affinity and drains session-bound KV caches before full cutover. Design highlights: - Cohort selection: configurable cohort selectors (percent-based, geo, header-pinned, experiment IDs). - Telemetry aggregation: new streaming aggregator produces rolling risk scores per cohort combining latency P50/P95/P99 deltas, error-rate deltas, structured-output drift (via lightweight token-diff heuristics), and eval-set probe results. - Handover latches: latch tokens tied to session IDs ensure in-flight sessions complete on the original model until a drain-window completes; new 'stitch' call in the service API acts as the atomic handoff point. - Safety gates: multi-signal gating with hysteresis, optional manual holdpoints, automatic rollback triggers on expedited regression patterns. - Observability: per-cohort dashboards and a 'handover timeline' trace in the Console showing sweep metrics, pass/fail reasons and KV-cache drain durations. Backwards compatibility: Adapter plugs into the existing rollout runtime via a new adapter interface; if disabled, orchestrator falls back to legacy phased promotion. Tests & validation: - Unit tests for risk-score math and latch semantics. - Integration tests with the shadow bridge harness to validate mirrored traffic sweep and stitch sequence. - Load test in perf-canary that simulates 5000 RPS mixed cohorts verifying p95 latency and drain correctness. - End-to-end dry-run against a staging model using synthetic eval probes. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind "sweep_stitch_adapter" feature flag and config defaults disabled. - Phased canary: start with 1 customer org on dedicated staging, then 10 internal orgs, then broader. - Monitoring playbook added: alert on stitch failures, reversion events, or prolonged latch durations (>30s). Related work: builds on earlier shadow-verifier and cohort-handshake work (ENG-6121) and ties to the telemetry aggregation pieces in ENG-6932. Motivation ticket: SUP-3321. Implementation notes: - Runtime changes in runtime/service: introduce StitchCoordinator and lightweight in-memory cohort state cache. - Observability in console: new timeline visualization component and per-cohort panel. - API: small addition to rollout API: POST /rollouts/{id}/stitch to trigger the final handover (internal use only). - Security: stitch operations require rollout.write permission; audit events emitted for every stitch and rollback. Operational considerations: - Handover latch increases short-term memory usage to maintain session mappings for the drain window; configured default latch TTL is 60s. - To minimize cost, the sweep phase samples mirrored traffic with adaptive sampling driven by request diversity heuristics.

review_comments: Amit Varma: Strong idea. Please add more detail on how risk-score weights are tuned and whether they can be overridden per-customer. Also add a fallback path if the latency signal is noisy.
Riley Chen (author): Added per-customer overrides and a default noise-resistant rolling-mean for latency; documented fallback behavior (legacy phased promote) in the design doc.
Sofia Patel: Concern about latch TTL causing memory retention on busy hosts. Can we make latch TTL adaptive based on session length percentiles?
Riley Chen (author): Implemented adaptive TTL tied to 95th percentile session duration with a max cap; added config knobs and tests.
Jun Park: Tests look good; observed a flaky test in the shadow bridge harness under high concurrency. Please stabilize before merge.
Riley Chen (author): Fixed harness race by introducing deterministic request ordering in the test; re-ran perf canary.
Amit Varma: Approved after fixes. Sofia Patel: Approved. Jun Park: Approved.

ci_summary: All checks passed on final run: unit, integration, lint, typecheck, e2e-smoke. Perf canary completed and within acceptable latency/cost budgets.
hotfix_note: Not a hotfix. Feature gated and behind config; safe to revert via rollout API or feature flag.
operational_playbook: Added Playbook: On stitch failures check aggregator signals (latency, error spikes, structured diff), examine latch drain durations, if automated rollback triggered inspect snapshot logs and optionally re-run sweep with increased sampling. Contact oncall: #sre-rollouts.
